method: Consumer-product circle of competence. Inclusion requires more than product familiarity: observing the customer experience must help explain the causal earnings engine through demand, frequency, pricing, retention, throughput, unit economics, or brand strength. Direct contact with an enterprise tool, exchange, broker, or infrastructure product does not qualify when the decisive revenue and margin drivers remain opaque. This is a research-priority map, not a valuation screen or recommendation list.
context_used: The user explicitly prefers product-centric, consumer-facing businesses over enterprise and market-infrastructure companies
The user identified CME as the defining counterexample: using the product does not mean understanding what makes the business improve or deteriorate
Product observation should connect to demand, frequency, pricing, retention, throughput, unit economics, or brand strength
Direct use alone is insufficient when revenue mix, regulation, capital intensity, enterprise sales, or financial plumbing dominate the economics
No company is assumed to be a product the user personally uses unless that has been explicitly established

companies.why_fit: The product promise is concrete: limited assortment, sharp prices and a membership customers choose to renew. Traffic, basket, renewal and perceived value connect directly to the earnings model.
companies.hard_part: The stock can price in extraordinary durability long before the operating evidence changes, and gasoline, FX and merchandise mix can blur the clean story.
companies.first_kpis: Traffic; comparable sales ex-fuel/FX; membership renewal; fee income; gross margin; inventory

companies.why_fit: Food quality, wait times, throughput, price, traffic and new-store execution are visible. Those observations map cleanly to same-store sales, restaurant margin and unit growth.
companies.hard_part: Food and labor inflation, digital mix, cannibalization and a premium valuation can outweigh an otherwise good customer experience.
companies.first_kpis: Transactions; price/mix; comparable sales; throughput; restaurant margin; openings; average unit volume

companies.why_fit: Engagement, habit formation, product quality, ad load and willingness to pay can be tested directly. Those behaviors feed users, conversion, retention and subscription revenue.

excluded.reason: That usage does not reveal rate per contract, product mix, open-interest quality, collateral income, incentive programs or regulatory competition. This is the defining example of familiarity without business understanding.
excluded.what_would_change_mind: A short causal model that predicts revenue and margins from volume, mix, RPC, open interest and collateral balances.

excluded.what_would_change_mind: A reliable bridge from accounts, client equity, DARTs and rate assumptions to pretax profit.
